definition: Language planning is the way a state or other institutions deliberately shape how a language is used, supported, and developed in society. In this source, it refers especially to moving beyond simple protection of a language toward strengthening its role and competitiveness in digital, educational, and public life.

reasons: The definition says language planning involves “the way a state or other institutions deliberately shape how a language is used, supported, and developed.” The packet specifically mentions the state regulating language planning, but does not support the inclusion of “other institutions,” nor does it clearly support shaping “how a language is used, supported, and developed” in those exact terms.

The second sentence claims the source “refers especially to moving beyond simple protection of a language toward strengthening its role and competitiveness in digital, educational, and public life.” The packet supports moving from “traditional language protection” toward “active construction of digital sovereignty,” and it supports competitiveness in the digital/AI age and mentions educational materials and academic/technical digital content; however, “public life” is not explicitly supported in the packet.
